title: AI agents are getting their own desks
content: On 8 October 2026 Google Cloud announced a universal AI agent for the workplace at its Gemini at Work 2026 event.

title: A coworker, not just a chatbot
content: Google says the agent can research, create documents, write code, coordinate other agents and complete tasks that last hours or days.

title: Its own email address
content: A coworker agent can receive its own Workspace account, email address, calendar, Drive storage and a place in the company directory, VentureBeat reported.

title: Give it a goal, get finished work
content: Users hand one agent an objective; it decides how to complete it, reaches into company systems and returns finished work.

title: It remembers who it is
content: The agent keeps the same memory, business context and identity across apps and devices.

title: No new app to learn
content: It works through Gemini Enterprise and familiar tools such as Google Workspace, Microsoft 365 and Slack rather than a dedicated app.

title: The story in one line
content: The big AI platforms are turning agents into persistent digital colleagues with their own identities, inboxes and budgets.

title: Assistant or coworker
content: Agents can be set up as personal assistants or as persistent coworkers with shared team responsibilities.

title: The Event Planner Agent
content: VentureBeat's example is an "Event Planner Agent" with its own Workspace identity.

title: Assign work in chat
content: Employees can give it work by mentioning it in Google Chat or asking it to edit a document.

title: Runs in the cloud
content: Tasks run in the cloud, so you can start on one device and pick up on another without rebuilding context.

title: Multi-day workflows
content: The agent can manage workflows over several days, run assignments in parallel and react to schedules or events.

title: It builds its own teams
content: It can assemble temporary teams of specialised sub-agents and split responsibilities between them.

title: Everywhere you work
content: One interface and API span the web, iOS, Android, Windows, Mac and command-line tools.

title: Not only Gemini
content: The agent already supports Anthropic's Claude models, with more proprietary and open-weight models planned.

title: Four kinds of memory
content: Google describes session, semantic, procedural and episodic memory for its agents.

title: Session memory
content: Session memory tracks the tasks currently in progress.

title: Semantic memory
content: Semantic memory holds knowledge the agent builds up over time.

title: Procedural memory
content: Procedural memory stores workflows the agent has learned.

title: Episodic memory
content: Episodic memory records the agent's previous work.

title: A verifiable identity
content: Each agent has a cryptographically attested identity, with permissions managed through enterprise security systems.

title: Everything is logged
content: Agent actions go into audit logs, including when it creates isolated environments to run code.

title: An Agent Gateway
content: An Agent Gateway enforces company-wide policies on how agents talk to outside systems.

title: Sandboxed code
content: Sandboxing limits what code the agent can run.

title: Only what you share
content: Coworker agents can reach only information team members explicitly share, rather than inheriting a person's full permissions.

title: Spending caps
content: Project-level spending limits can pause an agent when its budget runs out, and costs can be charged to departments.

title: Smart Routing
content: Smart Routing picks a model for each workload based on performance and cost.

title: Plugs into business software
content: Supported tools include Salesforce, ServiceNow, Jira, Git, BigQuery, Snowflake, Databricks and Microsoft Teams.

title: MCP built in
content: Companies can connect Model Context Protocol servers and publish reusable instructions and tools to internal registries.

title: Finance agents
content: A Financial Services offering in preview includes more than 50 foundational skills and connects to FactSet and LSEG.

title: Legal agents
content: The Legal offering supports NetDocuments and iManage, with a focus on document permissions and confidentiality.

title: Most of the Fortune 100
content: Google says nearly 90% of Fortune 100 companies use Gemini Enterprise.

title: BNP Paribas: 65,000 staff
content: BNP Paribas is rolling Gemini Enterprise out to more than 65,000 employees.

title: SOMPO: 10,000 agents
content: Japanese insurer SOMPO has built more than 10,000 custom agents.

title: Those numbers are for the old product
content: These figures describe the existing Gemini Enterprise product, not necessarily the new universal agent.

title: No price yet
content: Google has not announced a separate price for the universal agent.

title: No launch date
content: Google has not given a general-availability date or said whether existing subscriptions include it.

title: Licensing questions
content: Google has not said how agent accounts will be provisioned or licensed, or whether every agent needs its own Workspace seat.

title: No independent tests
content: Google has not published independent benchmarks of how reliably the agent handles long, cross-application tasks.

title: Microsoft Autopilot
content: On 25 September Microsoft announced Copilot Autopilot, which runs in the background with its own identity, memory and workspace. It is in private preview.

title: OpenAI Dots
content: At DevDay on 29 September OpenAI introduced Dots, always-on agents that work across connected apps.

title: Anthropic in Google Docs
content: On 6 October Anthropic launched Claude integration with Google Docs, Sheets and Slides.

title: Grok Team Bots
content: SpaceXAI's Team Bots, persistent agents with their own cloud computers, entered public beta on 28 September.

title: Everyone wants the always-on agent
content: Within about two weeks, Microsoft, OpenAI and Google all announced persistent agents with their own identity or memory.

title: Agents are targets too
content: At Pwn2Own Ireland 2026, researchers exploited 32 unique zero-days and earned $388,500 on the opening day, Cyber Security News reported.

title: OpenAI Codex fell
content: Ikotas Labs exploited OpenAI Codex with a single argument-injection flaw and earned $40,000.

title: LiteLLM fell twice
content: Taisic Yun of Xint got a reverse shell on LiteLLM for $40,000, and Out of Bounds exploited it through four bugs for $15,000.

title: An AI database too
content: VinSOC chained five flaws in Oracle's Autonomous AI Database for $40,000.

title: Contest, not attacks
content: These demonstrations took place under contest rules and are not evidence of attacks on real users.

title: Why identity matters
content: An agent with its own inbox and file access is a new account to secure, which is why attested identity, audit logs and gateways feature so heavily.

title: Pricing and seats
content: Watch how Google prices agent accounts and whether they count as Workspace seats.

title: Real-world reliability
content: Watch for independent tests of multi-day agent work.

title: Admin controls
content: Watch whether admins can switch individual Workspace features on or off for agents.

title: Snapshot date
content: This pack reflects sources opened on 9 October 2026. Later evidence should go in a new dated pack.
